title: Almost-linear exact directed global minimum cut
formal: For every fixed integer \(a\ge1\), is there a uniform bounded-error randomized word-RAM algorithm that, on every directed graph with positive integer arc weights at most \(n^{a}\), outputs a nonempty proper set \(S\subset V\) minimizing \(\sum_{e\in E(S,V\setminus S)}u_{e}\), and its exact value, in \((m+n)^{1+o(1)}\) worst-case time?
definitions: The graph is given by its vertex set \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), with \(n\ge2\), and an explicit list of \(m\) arcs. It has no loops and at most one arc per ordered pair; opposite arcs are allowed. Here \(E(S,V\setminus S)\) consists of arcs directed from \(S\) to its complement, and the objective counts each such arc once. There are no prescribed terminals. Zero optimum is allowed, including when the graph is not strongly connected. Weights are explicitly given integers in \(\{1,\ldots,n^{a}\}\). Use a uniform word RAM with word length \(w=d\lceil\log_{2}(n+2)\rceil\), for a fixed positive integer \(d\) chosen with the algorithm and large enough for its addresses and input values. Unit-cost instructions are word reads/writes, copying, comparisons, branching, Boolean operations, shifts, addition, subtraction and multiplication modulo \(2^{w}\), and integer quotient and remainder with nonzero divisor. Shifts by at least \(w\) return zero. Multiword computation is charged by its component instructions. The fixed finite program receives no advice or precomputed tables; all initialization, preprocessing and output writes count. Randomness consists of independent uniform random words, each generated at unit cost. On every input, the whole output must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\). The time bound holds for every random execution, including unsuccessful ones. Write \(N=m+n\). Almost-linear time means that there exist one algorithm, a constant \(C\) and a function \(h:\mathbb{N}\to[1,\infty)\), independent of the input graph, with \(\lim_{N\to\infty}\log h(N)/\log N=0\), such that the time is at most \(CNh(N)\) for every input. All hidden constants are independent of the graph. The program, word-size constant, overhead function and time constant may depend on \(a\), but not on the graph or its weights.

context_blocks.text: A directed global cut identifies the cheapest partition across which communication in one direction can be removed. The terminal pair is unknown, unlike a single source–sink flow problem.

Quanrud and independently Mosenzon obtain almost-linear approximation schemes. Their bounds depend inversely on the relative error parameter, so exact recovery of a large integer optimum need not retain almost-linear time.
The target asks for the optimal cut itself and its exact value over all partitions. It isolates the global directed-cut bottleneck after the major progress on exact single-pair flow.

why: Exact global directed connectivity is a fundamental graph optimization problem whose unknown optimal terminals remain a major obstacle beyond fast single-pair flow.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the specified model, quantifiers and guarantees. A conditional lower bound settles only its conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean; a partial improvement does not meet the target.

The revised independent paper states \(O(m^{1+o(1)}/\varepsilon)\) time for polynomially bounded weights.

sentences: A directed global cut removes every arc leaving a chosen nonempty proper vertex set.
The task is to minimize its total weight without being given source and sink terminals.
The question asks for exact almost-linear computation with bounded-error randomization and polynomially bounded integer weights.
Known almost-linear approximation schemes retain a precision cost that matters for exact recovery.
A resolution would address the global directed-cut bottleneck beyond single-pair maximum flow.
